converse.emptyText: Pick a graph and type. The canvas follows the session when it is the graph you have open.
converse.emptyVoice: Press start and say something. What you say appears as you speak it.
converse.halfDuplexHelp: Stops the microphone while the assistant talks. Use it if the assistant interrupts itself through your speakers; headphones solve the same problem.
converse.insecureContext: A microphone needs a secure context. localhost works; a LAN address over plain http:// does not — use https or open the UI on the machine itself.
converse.requires: Needs a microphone and the voice graph running: expertise/asr, expertise/llm-chat, expertise/sentence-chunker and expertise/tts.
converse.voiceGraphHelp: Voice runs the `voice` graph: speech to text, a model, a sentence chunker and speech synthesis, all at once.

graphs.subtitle: Registered graphs — declared by a person or compiled by the planner.

projections.subtitle: Existing systems exposed as Expertise — no code changes on their side.
projections.name: Name (optional)
projections.baseUrl: Base URL (optional if the spec declares servers)
projections.empty: No projections yet. Connect an existing API and its operations become Expertise.
projections.writeWarning: live mode performs REAL writes on the target system

reference.undocumented: The binary offers commands the guide does not document: {{list}}. Run scripts/gen_ui_reference.py after documenting them.
reference.enumsLead: The contract enumerations, from spec/enums.yaml — the same file the kernel's Go constants, the Python tuples and the SDK's TypeScript unions are generated from. What is listed here is what the kernel accepts.

sessions.emptyHelp: Open one from the Studio's Run panel, or with `aura chat --graph echo "hello"`.
sessions.pick: Each one opens as its causal tree: every envelope under the one that caused it, on a time axis.
sessions.openGraph: Open this graph in the Studio
sessions.tokensHelp: Summed from attest.usage on the envelopes that carry it. An Expertise that reports no usage contributes nothing.
sessions.noTraceHelp: The client sent no traceparent, so no envelope of this session carries one.
sessions.searchEvents: Search node, port, text, id, receipt
sessions.capped: The node returns at most {{n}} events per session; this view shows that many.
sessions.streamHelp: {{count}} envelopes on this port with the same cause, shown as one row
sessions.suppressedHelp: Logged after its chain was cancelled. The work ran; the kernel routed its output nowhere.
sessions.sealedHelp: The kernel sealed this delivery in the effect ledger.
sessions.elidedHelp: On a realtime edge the kernel logs the envelope and its hash, not the payload.

studio.badRef: "{{ref}}" is not a usable ref: lowercase letters, digits, - and _, and not already taken.
studio.cannotSplice: {{name}} has no input or no output, so nothing can pass through it.
studio.copiedIR: Graph IR copied to the clipboard.
studio.empty: State a goal above. The planner picks the Expertise, compiles a graph, and it appears here — then lights up as it runs.
studio.hint: Pick an Expertise from the palette, or double-click the canvas to add one where you click. Drag an output port to an input to wire an edge. Shift-drag selects a region, the wheel zooms, ? lists every shortcut.

history.empty: Nothing registered yet. A version is recorded the first time this graph is registered, and again whenever its content changes.
history.note: Loading a version does not roll the node back. Register it and the history gains an entry saying you went back — which is what happened.
history.restored: Loaded version #{{n}} onto the canvas. Register it to make it current.
history.title: {{graph}} — every version registered

inspector.clientNote: The client pseudo-node is the external application connection. C2 implies it from the edges that name it, so it is never written into nodes[] and cannot be removed.
inspector.deadlineHelp: How long a delivery here is worth waiting for. Absolute once on the wire; a later hop may tighten it, never extend it.
inspector.gateHelp: human-approval holds the message until a person confirms. Node policy may add one regardless; a graph can ask for more scrutiny, never less.
inspector.gateMotorHelp: This destination acts on the world. C2 rule 5 means the kernel adds a human-approval gate when none is declared — in published mode it refuses the session instead.
inspector.nothing: Select a node or an edge to see what it declares.
inspector.priorityHelp: Higher wins when two chains contend for the same Expertise.
inspector.qosRealtime: datagram; cannot stall or be stalled
inspector.qosReliable: one ordered stream, FIFO per edge
inspector.refHelp: This node's local name inside the graph. Lowercase, digits, dash or underscore.
inspector.resolveHelp: A demand the kernel satisfies at instantiation. Prefer this over a package: it lets the node degrade to another provider.
inspector.speculativeHelp: Deliver on partial upstream output and discard the work if the final output differs. Refused into a motor Expertise, and refused alongside a human-approval gate.
inspector.useHelp: Pin an exact package instead of a capability. Overrides resolve.

live.title: Running now

studio.notIR: That is not a C2 graph document (no "ir": "1").

studio.pastedIR: Loaded {{id}} from the clipboard. Register it to make it real.
studio.pinned: Pinned {{ref}}: its last output stands in for it, and the Expertise will not run.
studio.pinnedEmpty: Pinned {{ref}} with an empty payload — run the graph once, then pin again to capture a real output.
studio.placeholder: Describe a goal and the planner builds the graph — e.g. rank which models fit on this machine
studio.planTimeout: timed out waiting for the plan
studio.replicasHelp: This Expertise has more than one process connected. The kernel spreads sessions across them.
studio.sideHint: Select a node or edge to inspect it. Planner progress, results and approval gates of a run started here land in this pane. To talk to the graph and watch it, use Run.

edge.holding: The kernel is holding a delivery here for a person

help.unknown: Waiting for the node to answer /healthz.
help.down: The node is not answering. Start it with `aura up`; this page reconnects on its own.

palette.title: Command palette

token.title: Node token
token.needed: This node requires a bearer token and the request went out without a valid one.
token.have: A token is stored for this tab. Paste another to replace it.
token.none: No token is stored. A node started with --no-auth does not need one.

token.help: Kept in sessionStorage: it is gone when the tab closes and is never written to the URL.

pulse.unsupported: Pulse reads everything from that route, which this node's version predates. Sessions, Evidence and the Studio work as before.
pulse.stale: Last poll failed, showing the previous sample: {{message}}
pulse.sessionsChart: Live sessions over the last 90 seconds
pulse.cacheSub: {{cached}} of {{input}} input tokens served from cache
pulse.approvalsOff: this node has no approval queue
pulse.approvalsWaiting: held by the kernel for a person — open the inbox
pulse.inferencesSub: replies that reported usage, since start
pulse.loadNote: one bar per connection; height is its live sessions
pulse.spreadHelp: Busiest replica minus idlest. Load-aware routing keeps this at 0 or 1.
pulse.mailboxInline: Inline dispatch (--session-mailbox 0): no mailboxes in use.
pulse.waitsHelp: Times a full mailbox made the connection's read loop wait.
pulse.droppedHelp: Envelopes that arrived for a session that had already ended.
pulse.specSub: of resolved speculative deliveries were right
pulse.refusedHelp: Speculation the kernel would not start, e.g. into a motor Expertise.
pulse.batchHelp: Rows per commit. Above 1 means group commit is combining concurrent writers.
pulse.about: AURA is the operating system for autonomous robots. This node runs live graphs of Expertise — perception, decision, actuation, memory — over typed streams, holds every actuation for its gate, and seals it in the ledger.
pulse.cutOffHelp: Observers the node disconnected because they could not keep up.

evidence.sound: The ledger verifies: {{count}} entries, chain intact
evidence.sound_one: The ledger verifies: {{count}} entry, chain intact
evidence.noKey: node key not available: signatures were not checked
evidence.noLedger: This node has no effect ledger
evidence.noQueue: This node has no approval queue
evidence.noQueueHelp: A gate reaching a programmatic client is then denied.
evidence.search: Filter by capability, session, approver, receipt
evidence.unsignedHelp: A person answered the gate without a signed approval, so the entry records the decision and not who made it.
evidence.emptyHelp: An entry is written each time the kernel delivers into, or refuses to deliver into, a motor.* Expertise.
evidence.approved: Approved. The kernel delivers and seals it.
evidence.denied: Denied. The kernel seals the refusal; nothing is delivered.
evidence.inboxNote: Gates raised for a client that is not a person (an MCP caller, a webhook). A gate inside an interactive session is answered in that session — in the Studio's Run panel — and does not appear here.
evidence.inboxEmptyHelp: The kernel is not holding any delivery for a human.
evidence.needsSigned: This node's policy requires a signed approval that binds what the operator was shown ({{labels}}). A browser holds no operator key, so it cannot be answered here: run `aura approve {{id}} --as <operator>`.
evidence.unsignedNote: Answered from here it is unsigned: the ledger records the decision, not your identity. `aura approve {{id}} --as <operator>` signs it.
